## Build GUI binding using Gradle

The `llama.android` directory contains a Gradle build script that can be used to build the project.

```sh
# Build the project
./gradlew build

# Run the project
./gradlew run
```

## Build GUI binding using CMake

The `llama.android` directory contains a CMake build script that can be used to build the project.

```sh
# Build the project
cmake -B build -G "Unix Makefiles"
cmake --build build

# Run the project
./build/llama.android
```

## Build GUI binding using Make

The `llama.android` directory contains a Makefile that can be used to build the project.

```sh
# Build the project
make

# Run the project
./llama.android
```

## Build GUI binding using Python

The `llama.android` directory contains a Python script that can be used to build the project.

```sh
# Build the project
python build.py

# Run the project
./llama.android
```

- **For Ubuntu 24.04**

The release packages for Ubuntu 24.04 x64 (FP32/FP16) only include the binary files of the llama.cpp SYCL backend. They require the target machine to have pre-installed Intel GPU drivers and oneAPI packages that are the same version as the build package. To get the version and installation info, refer to [.github/workflows/release.yml#L713](../../.github/workflows/release.yml#L713): ubuntu-24-sycl -> Download & Install oneAPI.

It is recommended to use them with [Intel Docker](https://hub.docker.com/r/intel/deep-learning-essentials).
